_comment: Deploy to \NVRAM\intercomConfig.json on the processor. REQUIRED for door video. This was once only a fallback behind the video url the panel reports itself (VOIPVideoURLFeedback) - that member DOES NOT EXIST on these panels, confirmed by dumping the live extender on a TST-1080, so the url configured here is the only way to get a picture. Everything else on the intercom page (answer/reject/hangup/DND/mute) works without this file.
_comment2: THE VALUES BELOW ARE THE REAL ONES, read off a live call on 2026-08-06 - not examples. The console logged: name="2N IP Verso" num="sip:111@192.168.1.1". sipNumber is matched against the USER PART of that URI, so it is 111, not the whole URI. name is matched as a case-insensitive SUBSTRING OF the incoming display name, so it must be contained in "2N IP Verso" - 'Front Door' would never match, which is why the shipped example did not.
_comment3: ⚠ NAME IS THE MATCH THAT ACTUALLY FIRES. On the first frame of an incoming call the panel reports num="" - the caller URI does not arrive until the call is ANSWERED. Video is resolved at the incoming transition (deliberately: the url must be set before the page flip), so at that moment there is no number to match on. Name matching, or the single-station fallback, is what resolves it. Do not remove either believing sipNumber covers it.
_comment4: ⚠ USE THE PRESET PATH /h264_stream. The parameterised form the 2N documents - rtsp://192.168.1.243/media?vcodec=h264&vres=640x480&fps=15&vbr=2000&audio=1 - would NOT open in VLC on 2026-08-06 (it appeared to want credentials that the web-GUI login did not satisfy), while rtsp://192.168.1.243/h264_stream opened straight away with no auth. Do not 'improve' this back to the parameterised url. Consequence: the stream's resolution/fps/bitrate now come from the 2N's own settings, NOT from the url - so they must be set in the 2N web UI (Services > Streaming, and the Video tab). Panels need H.264 and will NOT decode H.265; 2N/Crestron recommend 640x480 @ 30fps, 2048 kbps. RTSP needs the 2N Enhanced Video licence.
_comment5: IF THE PANEL SHOWS NOTHING, isolate with a stream known to render on these panels: 'intercomvideo 12 rtsp://192.168.1.222:7447/7cvhHLy1cHpVg6bZ' - the UniFi Front Door camera from cameraConfig.json. If that appears and the 2N does not, the fault is the 2N (codec/licence/sessions), not the page. Either way watch the console for 'INTERCOM TP-n ch5-video state/errorCode' - the decoder says why. NOTE that VLC opening a stream does NOT mean a panel will: VLC decodes H.265 and the panels do not.
_comment7: ⚠ MULTICAST. Unicast RTSP is limited by the 2N's simultaneous-session count: with two panels ringing, the second was refused with errorCode 56532 'Request for greater than maximum simultaneous sessions per device' and showed no picture. Multicast has no per-viewer session at all, so every ringing panel can show the door. Nothing in the PROGRAM changes - put the multicast url in rtspUrl below exactly as you would a unicast one; it is passed to ch5-video verbatim. Configure the multicast address on the 2N (Services > Streaming), give EACH door station its own unique multicast address, and keep the codec H.264.
_comment8: ⚠ MULTICAST NETWORK CAVEAT - it is only more robust if the network is set up for it. Without IGMP snooping (and an IGMP querier somewhere on the VLAN) a multicast video stream is flooded to every switch port, which degrades the whole network rather than just the intercom. Confirm the switches handle IGMP before assuming multicast is the safer option. If in doubt on a small house with one or two panels, unicast is genuinely simpler.
_comment6: type selects the INTERCOM SCENARIO (page layout): 'sip' = scenario 1, a SIP/Rava station (2N Verso) with full call control via the panel's VOIP extender. 'unifi' = scenario 2, a view-only station (UniFi G6 Entry): RTSP video+audio, no SIP session, so no answer/reject/hangup/mic - just video and Dismiss. Defaults to 'sip' when omitted.
